stories.title: US scientists drop poisoned mice from helicopters to fight invasive snakes in Guam
stories.description: US scientists are dropping dead mice laced with painkillers over Guam's forests to control invasive snakes threatening native wildlife and power lines
stories.excerpt: U.S. scientists are dropping dead mice containing paracetamol from helicopters over Guam's forests in an effort to bring down populations of invasive brown tree snakes that have devastated native wildlife and disrupted electricity supplies on the Pacific island. The unusual method, developed by researchers working with the U.S. Department of Agriculture's Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS), uses dead mice fitted with 80-milligram paracetamol tablets, a common painkiller that is toxic to the snakes. The poisoned bait is released from helicopters using parachute-like devices designed to catch on tree branches, where the snakes live and hunt. Brown tree snakes are believed to have arrived on Guam aboard cargo ships in the late 1940s or early 1950s, following World War II. stories.excerpt: People stopped for minor traffic violations will no longer be referred to US Immigration and Customs Enforcement. The mayor of Houston, the most populous city in the US state of Texas, has ordered the city’s police force to sharply limit its cooperation with the United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). John Whitmire’s executive order came on Friday, days after Democrats swept statewide offices in the traditionally Republican state. According to the order, Houston police will contact ICE only when a person is being arrested for a jailable offence, according to the Reuters news agency. Whitmire said he had consulted Texas’s newly elected governor, lieutenant governor and comptroller before acting, and that the move was meant to reduce fear and anxiety across the city. “Elections matter,” Whitmire told reporters. “I do this to begin a healing process,” he said, adding he hoped his executive order would become a model for other Texas cities. Giant pandas Ping Ping and Fu Shuang delighted visitors to Zoo Atlanta during their public debut Friday, chewing bamboo and lounging in their new US habitat while on loan from China. A male named Ping Ping and female Fu Shuang arrived from Chengdu in September via a FedEx flight dubbed the "Panda Express", and are to be hosted in the southern US facility for the next 10 years. Peña was arrested on Friday minutes after lawmakers, including from his own party, unanimously voted to remove him from office following the collapse earlier this week of Ueno Bank, which has links to his private business interests. He had offered to step down on Thursday. Rather than accept his resignation, senators impeached Peña and charged him with misconduct, meaning he has been stripped of the immunity usually granted to ex-presidents. Peña, who until last year held shares in the company that owned the bank, has denied any wrongdoing.
